known_gaps.scope_clause: 'questions about countries outside the donor panel'
known_gaps.why: The donor panel is 99 candidate countries and the corpus names none of them — it says "99 candidate countries x 5 screening predictors". The country list lives in the acquisition manifest under `data/`, which is gitignored, so a rule built on it would behave differently on a fresh clone than on this machine and the published metric would not be reproducible. Until the panel's membership is committed as an artifact, the class is declared and undetected.

known_gaps.scope_clause: the whole of the answer contract's post-check
known_gaps.why: The gate decides an intent and a citation. It does not assemble an answer, so it cannot check an answer for an interval, an identifying assumption and a citation (R-04). That check belongs to the answer layer, which is not built.

The gate matches literal patterns, so a paraphrase that avoids the declared words is not detected. The alternative — a classifier trained on the eval set — would score better on the eval set and mean less, and the project's rule is that a number must not be tuned into existence.

G05 refuses a value at a year outside the window, and G02 refuses a question that forecasts in words. A question that asks for a value in a year the window covers but the outcome series does not (2025-2026) is left answerable, because the study window is open and the registry's own state in those years is answerable. The answer layer refuses it when no chunk answers it.
